A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReasonFlux-PRM work. All 30 pages, including equations, figures, tables, references and Appendices A–F, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 5 report original data-selection, supervised fine-tuning, GRPO and Best-of-N experiments. Appendices D–E include model-scaling results, combined SFT+RL experiments and scored case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–7, experimental figures and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same alignment, quality and coherence rewards, template-guided trajectory reward, joint training objective, and procedures for data selection, GRPO and Best-of-N inference.

E1.justification: The same s1/OpenThoughts data sources and MATH/DAPO RL data are described. Evaluation remains on AIME24, AIME25, MATH500 and GPQA-Diamond, with no added task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each experiment: offline selection retains Math-Shepherd, Skywork, Qwen PRMs, random selection and human curation; GRPO retains rule-based and Qwen PRM rewards; Best-of-N retains Qwen, Skywork and majority voting.

E3.justification: Sections 3–5 and Appendices A.1 and C retain the same model configurations, sample counts, training budgets and accuracy evaluations. Best-of-N still uses N = 2, 4, 8, 16 and temperature 0.3.

E4.justification: The alpha/beta ablations in Tables 4–5, efficiency analyses in Figures 8–9, model-scaling and SFT+RL analyses in Appendix D, and case studies in Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 3 states in both versions that accuracy is averaged over 16 independent runs. Repeated-run information, plotted uncertainty and other statistical reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: All table entries, plotted results and case-study scores match. For example, Table 2 retains 84.8 on MATH500 and 47.5 on GPQA-Diamond for ReasonFlux-PRM-7B-selected SFT, while Table 7 retains 89.8 for combined SFT+RL.

T1.justification: The trajectory-response definitions and assumptions in Section 2 and mathematical formulations in Equations 1–14 are unchanged. No theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same trajectory-aware reward-modeling contributions and application claims, including average improvements of 12.1% for SFT, 4.5% for RL and 6.3% for test-time scaling.

C2.justification: Interpretations of trajectory-response mismatch, reward weighting and efficiency are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same dependence on high-quality training pairs and qualifications about extending beyond structured mathematical and scientific reasoning.

D1.justification: Appendices A–C retain the same prompts, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions and implementation details. The documented code and model link targets are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 and all 69 reference entries match. Positioning relative to prior PRMs, distilled-data selection and test-time scaling remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 23 June 2025 to v2 dated 25 September 2025. Otherwise, the prose, terminology, headings and document structure match throughout the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–7 retain the same content, captions, designs and locations. Page organization is unchanged; negligible glyph-positioning differences do not amount to a layout revision.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and limitations are unchanged, including Appendices A–F. The updated version/date stamp and negligible rendering differences produce no meaningful net change in paper quality.
